title: Synthetic Data Augmentation for Functional Data: Wasserstein Risk Bounds and Diffusion-Based Conditional Generation
abstract: arXiv:2610.34120v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Functional data are costly to collect; samples of tens to hundreds of curves are common. Synthetic data augmentation can help, but its theory is developed for finite-dimensional data and relies on total variation, which is uninformative for functions. We study augmentation with a class-conditional functional diffusion generator and state guarantees in the Wasserstein-1 distance. For stable downstream estimators, we bound the risk of training on synthetic curves, from above and below, by the risk of training on as many real curves plus a generation penalty, and derive the best number of synthetic curves and a condition under which synthetic data outperform real data. For allocating synthetic curves under class imbalance, we bound the excess risk of training on real and synthetic curves together, without sample splitting. In applications to temperature, hyperspectral and gait curves, augmentation improved classification, function-to-scal

translated_title: 函数型数据的合成数据增强：Wasserstein风险界与基于扩散模型的条件生成
translated_abstract: 函数型数据的采集成本高昂，样本通常仅有数十到数百条曲线。合成数据增强可以缓解这一问题，但现有理论仅针对有限维数据发展而来，且依赖于全变差距离——而全变差对函数数据而言不具信息量。我们研究基于类条件函数型扩散生成器的数据增强方法，并以Wasserstein-1距离给出理论保证。对于稳定的下游估计器，我们从上界和下界两个方向将基于合成曲线训练的风险界定为基于相同数量真实曲线训练的风险加上一个生成惩罚项，并由此推导出最佳合成曲线数量，以及合成数据优于真实数据的条件。针对类别不平衡情形下合成曲线的分配问题，我们在无需样本分割的情况下，对同时使用真实与合成曲线训练的额外风险给出了界定。在温度、高光谱和步态曲线的实际应用中，数据增强提升了分类和函数到标量（回归）的性能。
tldr: 该论文首次为函数型数据的合成数据增强建立了基于类条件扩散生成器的理论框架，在Wasserstein-1距离下给出训练风险的上下界，推导出最优合成样本数量以及合成数据优于真实数据的条件，并在类别不平衡场景下给出了无需样本分割的额外风险保证。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes the first theoretical framework for synthetic data augmentation of functional data via class-conditional diffusion generators, providing Wasserstein-1 risk bounds from above and below, deriving the optimal number of synthetic curves and conditions under which synthetic data outperform real data, including excess risk guarantees for class-imbalanced allocation without sample splitting.
